title: Saving & Loading Model Weights 💾
description: Learn to save and load model state_dict for inference and resuming.

slides.title: Why Save Models? 🤔
slides.content:
# Persisting Your Work

After hours of training, you want to keep the weights for later use:
* **Inference**: use the model without retraining.
* **Resume training**: continue from where you left off.
* **Share**: distribute your model to others.

PyTorch uses Python's `pickle` format, but you can also save just the trained parameters.

slides.title: Saving state_dict
slides.codeSnippet:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

model = nn.Linear(10, 2)
torch.save(model.state_dict(), 'model_weights.pth')
print('Weights saved')

quizData.question: What does `model.state_dict()` contain?

options.text: A dictionary mapping layer names to parameter tensors

quizData.explanation: `state_dict()` returns an OrderedDict of parameter names to tensors.

slides.title: Loading state_dict
slides.content: Recreate the model architecture and load weights.
slides.codeSnippet:
model = nn.Linear(10, 2)  # same architecture
model.load_state_dict(torch.load('model_weights.pth'))
print('Weights loaded')
# Now ready for inference

quizData.question: What must match between saving and loading state_dict?
quizData.explanation: You must instantiate an identical model before loading its state_dict.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use `.pth` or `.pt` extension

Common convention for PyTorch checkpoint files, but any extension works.
